name: An Empirical Analysis of CodeQL False Positives and Query Refinements for Java Vulnerabilities
publication: Amirali Sajadi, Sakikat Dutta and Preethha Chatterjee · arXiv, manuscript 2026
description: The authors manually examined 500 CodeQL false positives in selected Java queries and identified causes such as blocked data flow, sanitization, harmless execution context and misidentified trust boundaries.
reviewSteps: Record false-positive causes by rule and add paired cases for proposed filters.
Measure recall after each rule refinement. The study covers selected CodeQL Java queries.

name: Understanding Industry Perspectives of Static Analysis Based Security Testing
publication: Amit Seal Ami, Kevin Moran, Denys Poshyvanyk và Adwait Nadkarni · IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, 2024
description: Interviews with 20 practitioners describe how teams choose and use static security testing tools and what they expect from coverage, false positives and false negatives.
reviewSteps: Report scan scope, skipped file types and coverage limitations.
Use the interviews to inform usability. Measure SrcAudit accuracy on labeled code separately.

name: A Critical Comparison on Six Static Analysis Tools: Detection, Agreement, and Precision
publication: Valentina Lenarduzzi, Savanna Lujan, Nyyti Saarimäki và Fabio Palomba · arXiv, 2021
description: The authors compare six static analyzers on 47 Java projects and manually evaluate sampled warnings. Different tools often flag different locations within similar issue categories.
reviewSteps: Compare tools on the same labeled cases and verify the evidence before merging findings.
The study includes Java code quality warnings. Confirm vulnerability findings separately.

name: Learning to Reduce False Positives in Analytic Bug Detectors
description: The study evaluates learning-based triage for static-analysis warnings and tests transfer between null-dereference and resource-leak findings.
reviewSteps: If evaluating ranking, keep lower-priority findings available and surface those with clear evidence first.
Validate the method on the target language and weakness category before applying its results.

name: A Systematic Evaluation of Static API-Misuse Detectors
publication: Sven Amann, Brass, Sarah Nadi, Tien N. Babbitt and Mira Mezini · IEE Transctions on Sport Engineringer, 2018 (author)
description: The authors introduce MuBench and an evaluation procedure for static Java API-misuse detectors. Valid alternate usage patterns are an important source of false positives.
reviewSteps: Check library documentation and include examples of valid aliases, configuration and default behavior.
Use cases from the target framework when evaluating rules outside the Java APIs studied.

name: Lessons from Building Static Analysis Tools at Google
publication: Caitlin Sadowski, Edward Aftandilian, Alex Eagle, Liam Miller-Cushon và Ciera Jaspan · Communications of the ACM, 2018
description: The authors describe how Google integrated static analysis into its development workflow and how engineers handled warnings during code review.
reviewSteps: Provide a location, explanation and actionable fix. Track feedback by rule.
Measure recall separately on labeled data.
